title: Muscles of the anterior and medial thigh (anterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Bodies and intervertebral discs of T12 to L5 and the transverse processes of the lumbar vertebrae.
Lesser trochanter of the femur, by a tendon shared with iliacus.
Anterior rami of L1 to L3.
With iliacus it is the strongest flexor of the thigh at the hip. With the limb fixed it flexes the trunk on the thigh, as in sitting up.
hy: Pus under its fascia (psoas abscess, classically from tuberculosis of the spine) can track down to the groin. Pain when the hip is extended is the psoas sign, also seen when an inflamed appendix lies against the muscle.

rows: Iliac fossa and the ala of the sacrum.
Lesser trochanter of the femur, with the tendon of psoas major.
With psoas major, flexes the thigh at the hip.
Anterior superior iliac spine and the front part of the iliac crest.
Iliotibial tract, which attaches to the lateral condyle of the tibia.
Flexes, abducts and medially rotates the thigh. Tightens the iliotibial tract, which steadies the extended knee.
Thickened lateral band of the fascia lata, from the iliac crest to the anterolateral (Gerdy) tubercle on the lateral condyle of the tibia.
Receives the insertions of tensor fasciae latae and most of gluteus maximus, and steadies the hip and the extended knee.
hy: Irritation where the tract crosses the lateral epicondyle of the femur, from friction or from compression of the tissue under it, causes pain on the outer side of the knee in runners and cyclists (iliotibial band syndrome).

rows: Upper part of the medial surface of the tibia, with gracilis and semitendinosus (pes anserinus).
Flexes, abducts and laterally rotates the thigh at the hip and flexes the leg at the knee, as in sitting cross-legged.
hy: The bursa under the pes anserinus can become inflamed and cause pain on the medial side of the knee.

rows: Anterior inferior iliac spine and the ilium just above the acetabulum.
Base of the patella through the quadriceps tendon, and through the patellar ligament the tibial tuberosity.
Extends the leg at the knee and helps flex the thigh at the hip. It is the only part of quadriceps femoris that crosses the hip.
hy: Tapping the patellar ligament makes quadriceps femoris contract: the knee jerk reflex, which tests the femoral nerve and the L2 to L4 segments, mainly L4.

rows: Greater trochanter and the lateral lip of the linea aspera of the femur.
Patella through the quadriceps tendon, and through the patellar ligament the tibial tuberosity.
Extends the leg at the knee.
Intertrochanteric line and the medial lip of the linea aspera of the femur.
Patella through the quadriceps tendon, and through the patellar ligament the tibial tuberosity.
Extends the leg at the knee. Its lowest fibers pull the patella medially and keep it in its groove.
Pectineal line on the superior ramus of the pubis.
Pectineal line of the femur, just below the lesser trochanter.
Femoral nerve (L2, L3); sometimes also a branch of the obturator nerve.
Adducts and flexes the thigh at the hip.
Body of the pubis, below the pubic crest.
Middle third of the linea aspera of the femur.
Body and inferior ramus of the pubis.
Upper part of the medial surface of the tibia, with sartorius and semitendinosus (pes anserinus).
Adducts the thigh, flexes the leg at the knee and helps rotate the flexed leg medially.
Anterior superior iliac spine to the pubic tubercle. It is the rolled-under lower edge of the aponeurosis of the external oblique.
Forms the floor of the inguinal canal. The femoral nerve, artery and vein and the iliopsoas pass under it into the thigh.
hy: It is the base of the femoral triangle; sartorius is the lateral border and adductor longus the medial border. Under it, from lateral to medial, lie the femoral nerve, artery and vein and then the lymphatics (NAVEL: Nerve, Artery, Vein, Empty space, Lymphatics).
A hernia that comes out above the ligament is inguinal. One that comes out below it, through the femoral canal, is femoral.
